answer.sourceLine: Unlike most feel-good lines pinned on famous names, this one really is Dolly’s — it is a signature personal motto she has shared on her official channels and is widely cited from her 2012 book Dream More. What we could not do is pin the exact first utterance to a dated primary document — and, contrary to popular belief, the phrase does not appear in the full transcript of her 2009 University of Tennessee commencement address.

source.excerpt: Find out who you are and do it on purpose.
trail: Goodreads attributes the line to Dolly Parton but, per its own disclaimer, names no book, speech, or date — a red flag that a quote is circulating without a source.
The line is genuinely hers: it is widely cited from her 2012 book Dream More, itself an expansion of her 2009 commencement remarks, and it appears on her verified official social accounts.
But it is not in the speech people credit: two full transcripts of the 2009 UT Knoxville address contain no such sentence, so its first documented utterance remains unpinned.
source.excerptNote: Dolly’s recurring shorthand for her whole philosophy of authenticity: know your own voice, then commit to it deliberately rather than imitating anyone else.

author.bio: Dolly Parton is one of the most successful and beloved figures in American music, the writer of standards such as “Jolene” and “I Will Always Love You,” and the founder of the Imagination Library children’s book charity. Beyond songwriting she is a prolific dispenser of homespun, self-deprecating wisdom — which is exactly why so many unsourced aphorisms also get pinned to her. This one, however, is a line she genuinely owns and repeats.

misattribution.intro: This is the unusual case: the attribution is right, but the source people give for it is wrong. The quote is genuinely Dolly Parton’s, yet it is routinely tied to a speech that does not contain it.

Sites such as Goodreads credit Dolly but attach no book, date, or context, leaving the exact origin floating.

misattribution.truthLine: It really is Dolly Parton’s line — a genuine personal motto cited from her 2012 book Dream More — just not, as commonly claimed, a line from her 2009 commencement address.

context.heading: Why it resonates
lead: Dolly Parton is one of the internet’s biggest magnets for invented wisdom, so the safe assumption for any clever line pinned to her is fabrication. This one survives the scrutiny: authenticity is the through-line of her entire public persona — the wigs, the rhinestones, the “it costs a lot of money to look this cheap” self-awareness — and “find out who you are and do it on purpose” is simply that philosophy compressed into nine words.

What we can’t give you is a clean birth certificate for the sentence. It is cited from her 2012 book Dream More and appears on her official accounts, but the specific first utterance — and the widespread claim that it comes from her 2009 commencement speech — do not hold up against the transcripts.
context.pull: Genuinely Dolly — just not from the speech everyone credits.
